messages:
maya: Heads up — we need per-route SLOs derived from traces for the new routing policy (fast/cheap/secure). Concern: exporter retention + sampling will muddy p95/p99. Any recommendations on deriving stable SLOs and wiring them into the console?

sam: +1. first step: tag spans with route_id and route_version. without route metadata it's impossible to attribute latency to routing decisions.

nate: Agree on tagging. Also think we should stop using raw spans directly for SLO windows. Emit derived latency metrics (histogram buckets) from spans at the collector and keep those in the metrics backend. That gives stable percentiles without storing all spans.

maya: can you sketch the otel collector config snippet we'd want?

sam: sample config (very rough):
```yaml
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc: {}
processors:
  attributes:
    actions:
      - key: route_id
        action: insert
      - key: model_family
        action: insert
  batch: {}
exporters:
  prometheus: {}
  otlp: {}
service:
  pipelines:
    metrics:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [attributes, batch]
      exporters: [prometheus]
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch]
      exporters: [otlp]
```

nate: The key is the metrics pipeline: create latency histograms with labels route_id, model_family, tenant_bucket. Compute error budget burn on those metrics. Keep raw spans short-term for debugging (e.g., 7–14d) and aggregated metrics longer.

irene: From the console UX side — we need those SLOs surfaced by default at route level, and an easy rollup toggle to show model_family or per-tenant (for enterprise customers). Also want deploy markers + error budget burn rate chart on the same view.

sam: two implementation notes: 1) route_id must be stable and owned by platform routing layer (no human-typed names). 2) to avoid cardinality explosion, only include tenant_id for premium plans (or bucket tenants into hashed cohorts).

maya: good call on cardinality. so SLO key becomes route_id + model_family by default. per-tenant SLOs opt-in.

nate: also keep in mind quotas: routing may fallback to cheaper model under quota pressure which changes latency distribution. SLO should be tied to the effective route+model variant used at serve time, otherwise you'll mask regressions. We need a route->model label on spans.

maya: agreed. action items from this thread:
- add route_id and model_family tags to span enrichment (sam)
- otelcol PR to emit latency histogram metrics (nate)
- retention proposal: raw spans 7d, tail traces 14d, derived metrics 90d (maya)
- console: add rollup toggles + deploy markers + per-tenant opt-in (irene)

maya: I'll open the tickets and assign owners.

deploy-bot: deploy started: otelcol/route-metrics -> staging :rocket:

sam: pinging on PR review when you see it, i'll test with the staging traffic spike tomorrow. :eyes:

maya: thanks — will post links to tickets and the trace->metric sample queries once PR lands. :thumbsup:
